title: Closing doxology and appeal to flee to Christ
english: If we are sick, let us flee to him. If our soul is in pain, let us follow the great physician of knowledge. If we hunger, let us receive the bread. If we have been put to death, let us take the resurrection. If we have grown old in ignorance, let us ask wisdom from wisdom itself.

But the word has drawn us out into a lengthy discourse, and perhaps we have become a hindrance to the fatherly teaching. The time now calls us to hear greater words as well, so that, helped by greater works, we may send up glory to God through our deeds. To him be glory both now and always and to the ages of ages. Amen.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.
baehrens: PG Homilia in paralyticum juxta piscinam jacentem u02-open
orientation: Cyril is closing the homily, urging his hearers to flee to Christ for every need and to glorify God through their deeds.
